reasons: The finding is correctly classified as 'missing': neither § 13 (Term) nor § 14 (Termination) imposes any data-return, export, deletion or transition-assistance obligation on TrueLink; § 13 only places migration burdens on Client (new name server within 30 days, new hosting environment within 60 days), confirming the gap in a hosting agreement holding Client Content and borrower/loan data.

The inserted paragraph tracks the playbook preferred position element-for-element: (a) up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates on Client's request, (b) return of Client data in a commonly used machine-readable format within thirty days, and (c) subsequent deletion with written certification.

The edit is an addition only — the existing § 14 sentence is left untouched — so it is the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position, and it uses contract-native party names (TrueLink/Client) and existing terminology (Client Content, with a clarifying reference to borrower and loan data) rather than generic Vendor/Customer placeholders.

The comment is accurate about what changed and why, cites the playbook requirement, and offers the 90-day fallback in the prescribed concise first-person-plural tone with the correct prefix; deterministic checks confirm the operation applies and the data-return/transition language is present.

Minor, non-blocking: the insertion relies on 'Client's Intellectual Property' and 'Client Proprietary Information' as defined terms that are not among the resolved definitions supplied — worth a quick capitalization/defined-term check against §§ 8–10 before sending, but the clause remains operative on 'other Client data' regardless.
